f186.summary: Baudouin-Desportes tells Aldobrandini that the papal commissaries Matteucci and Malvasia did more harm than the enemy, that the Spanish army stayed on the frontier, and that the Legate presses for a king's election just as the enemy wins votes by seeming to turn Catholic and "doit dimanche aller a la messe" (Henri IV heard Mass at Saint-Denis on Sunday 25 July). He recalls his requests in Rome and their refusal; Mayenne was willing to accept Guise as king. Reading by Paolo Rosson (v0.2, 1 Oct 2026) with Tomokiyo's key; the clear opening is only summarised in it.
f186.en:
⟨Clear opening, summarised only: "Most Illustrious Monseigneur, if I have not written to His Holiness and to Your Most
Illustrious Lordship as often as duty commands me, two things have prevented me ..." (uncertain events, unsafe roads);
"... In short, unless God sets His hand to it, I see the security of the Catholic religion in this kingdom in a bad way,
for several reasons I could tell Your Most Illustrious Lordship ..."; what the ministers "here for the Holy See" report
has nothing to do with the truth, "which will now be found such as I have always told it, at the"⟩ cost of my head.

Beginning with Monsieur Matteucci, down to the one who remains here, they alone have brought more ruin to our affairs
than the enemy, so full have they been of I know not what that does not suit us, or of small knowledge of our humours
and passions.

f189.summary: A letter in cover names ("nostre oncle", "l'homme de la chesne", "l'homme du colege", "nostre docteur Gratian"): the truce is expected "dans peu de jours", an envoy's journey "a fait changer de religion au [roy de Navarre]", and the Legate held back "nos brefz". Reading by Paolo Rosson (v0.2, 1 Oct 2026) with Tomokiyo's key.
f189.en:
⟨[J]uly 1593⟩

Our will was good, and our power great enough to make it succeed; but whether we could have held out in the long run,
that is what made us keep still. And meanwhile our friends showed themselves not only neutral but open enemies, and did
what they could to bring about the ruin of the [?friend] of the man of the College, and yours, sparing nothing, putting up
now one candidate, now another, seconded by our Doctor Gratian, who played the part better than any of the others, so
far as to stake his master's authority on it, indeed to compromise it and do it much harm. If our uncle had been willing
to speak according to the promise he had made to the man who went to see him, and if the man of the chain had given other
assurances than words, we would have gone in head down. But believe me, there was no thinking of it:

snip.cap: F. 189, the letter to Frachetta: Nostre volonté estoit bonne, la puissance asses grande pour la faire reussir opens the first line
snip.credit: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3984 f. 189 (Gallica btv1b9060633d view 353), reduced copy from P. Rosson’s repository

system: Catholic League polyphonic cipher: eleven glyphs each stand for two letters (a/n ... m/z), with signs for que, qui, pour and a few code signs.
